answer: A strong defence is to forge reputation that accrues slowly and cannot be bought: every agent earns trust only through verified, completed work, and each successful job adds a thin layer of credibility, like shale building up over time. If an attacker spawns many fake identities, each starts with zero reputation and no history, so creating a thousand of them costs real time and effort while yielding nothing. Any fraud then creates a ripple: one exposed identity drains the trust of every account linked to the same behaviour pattern, making a Sybil attack expensive, slow, and self-defeating.
